The Python and TypeScript clients. One client, one key, your memory.

For your first working example, follow the [quickstart](/build/getting-started/api-quickstart/). This page is
client reference: installation, configuration, methods and errors.

The SDK is a thin client over the Membase API. Every method is one operation of the
[API reference](/build/reference/api-reference/), and the access level, reach and confirmation rules are
enforced server-side, so the SDK cannot do anything the key cannot.

## Install


<Tabs syncKey="lang">


<TabItem label="Python">

```bash
pip install unibaseio-membase
```

Version 0.4.0 or newer. Python 3.10 or newer for the hosted client. One dependency, `httpx`.

For local mode, `pip install 'unibaseio-membase[local]'` on Python 3.12 or 3.13. It installs the
`unibaseio-membase-core` engine and runs memory on your machine; the engine calls a model
provider, by default OpenAI (`OPENAI_API_KEY`).

Local search returns results in retrieval order. To rerank them, set `MEMBASE_RERANK`:

- `llm`: one scoring call on your model provider, with the model you name in
  `MEMBASE_RERANK_LLM_MODEL`. Results that do not answer the question are dropped
  (`MEMBASE_RERANK_MIN_SCORE`, 0 to 10, default 3).
- `cross-encoder`: a local model you name in `MEMBASE_RERANK_CE_MODEL`, after
  `pip install sentence-transformers` (it installs torch).

To keep everything on the machine, point the engine at a local OpenAI-compatible server
such as [Ollama](https://ollama.com), for both chat and embeddings:

```bash
ollama pull qwen2.5:7b && ollama pull nomic-embed-text

export MEMBASE_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compat
export MEMBASE_LLM_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
export MEMBASE_EMBED_MODEL=nomic-embed-text MEMBASE_EMBED_DIM=768
export OPENAI_API_KEY=ollama   # the client needs a value; Ollama ignores it
for stage in READER RERANK EPISODE DECIDER AGENT KNOWLEDGE MULTIMODAL; do
  export MEMBASE_${stage}_MODEL=qwen2.5:7b
done
```

- Use `openai-compat`, not `MEMBASE_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama`: embeddings follow the endpoint only
  with `openai-compat`, and otherwise still go to OpenAI and need a real `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- `MEMBASE_EMBED_DIM` must match the embedding model, and a store keeps the width it was
  created with: switching embedding models means a new store.
- Every stage defaults to an OpenAI model name, so set each one, as above.
- Small models (around 3B) run but tend to embellish what they store; a 7B or larger instruct
  model keeps memories faithful.

With these set, `add`, `search`, `ask` and `membase --local mcp` make no calls beyond the
endpoint you named.

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="TypeScript">

```bash
npm install @unibaseio/membase
```

Version 0.4.0 or newer. Node 18 or newer (global `fetch`), Deno or Bun. Zero dependencies;
responses are typed.
The package is ESM only: from a CommonJS project, use an `.mts` file or set `"type": "module"`.

</TabItem>


</Tabs>


## Who owns the memory

In Membase **the person owns the memory**, not the app. A developer key is minted by the
account's owner under **Connect › Developer keys**, and it carries what they chose: an access
level, the Memories it may reach, whether it may read their profile, and when it expires. The
SDK takes that key and nothing else.

If you have used a memory API where you tag content with a *container tag* per end user and
one master key reaches them all: that is not this. No request names a Memory. Reads cover
every Memory the key reaches, and writes land in the key's **write target**: the one text
Memory it reaches. A Memory is one of the person's own topics, not a tenant, and answers name
it only for attribution (`memory_name`). A product that serves many people gives each of them
their own Membase account, and reaches their memory with their own key or their own consent. See [Multi-user Isolation](/build/guides/multi-user-isolation/).

## Create a client


<Tabs syncKey="lang">


<TabItem label="Python">

```python
from membase import Membase

client = Membase()                              # MEMBASE_API_KEY from the environment
client = Membase(api_key="mbk_…")               # or explicit
client = Membase(local=True)                    # local mode, in ~/.membase (MEMBASE_LOCAL=1 when no key is set)
```

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="TypeScript">

```ts
import { Membase } from "@unibaseio/membase";

const client = new Membase();                                    // MEMBASE_API_KEY from the environment
const explicit = new Membase({ apiKey: "mbk_…" });               // or explicit
const local = new Membase({ apiKey: "local", baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:8787" }); // `membase --local serve`
```

</TabItem>


</Tabs>


| Setting | Python | TypeScript | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request timeout | `timeout` (seconds) | `timeoutMs` (milliseconds) | 90 seconds |
| Retry limit | `max_retries` | `maxRetries` | 2 |
| API origin | `base_url` | `baseUrl` | `MEMBASE_BASE_URL`, else `https://api.app.membase.com` |

Releases before 0.4.0 speak the API this one replaced (they pass a `container` and read
`results`); upgrade both packages to 0.4.0 or newer.

A client for an API origin always needs a key: without `api_key` or `MEMBASE_API_KEY` the
constructor raises (`ValueError` in Python, `Error` in TypeScript), even when a base URL is
given. To talk to `membase --local serve` from either language, pass any key with
`http://127.0.0.1:8787`, or the value of `MEMBASE_LOCAL_TOKEN` when the server sets one.

Local memory (`Membase(local=True)` or `membase --local serve`) answers the same routes with the
same shapes. Its writes land in the store's write target, and a store with several Memories
needs `MEMBASE_WRITE_TARGET` set to the one writes go to.

Retries cover connection errors, timeouts, 408, 409, 429 and 5xx, with exponential backoff;
a numeric `Retry-After` is honoured when present (the server sends none today).
A cold runtime can take longer than the default timeout. See [API troubleshooting](/build/reference/troubleshooting/).
The method snippets below are independent examples; follow the quickstart to wait for an
accepted document to become searchable.

## The four verbs


<Tabs syncKey="lang">


<TabItem label="Python">

```python
# add: a document (its text, or a public url) into the key's write target. Answers 202 at once; learned in the background.
doc = client.add("Call notes with Acme: they want SSO before the pilot.",
                 title="Call with Acme", custom_id="call-2026-09-24")
doc["id"], doc["status"]                        # "doc_…", "pending" or "processing"; the same custom_id again starts nothing

# search: passages across every Memory in reach, most relevant first, each naming its Memory
hits = client.search("what does Acme need before the pilot", limit=5)
for h in hits["items"]:
    print(h["memory_name"], "·", h["content"])
hits["partial"]                                 # the Memories that could not answer

# profile: who the user is (needs the profile tick on the key)
p = client.profile(q="working hours")
p["static"], p["dynamic"], p["results"]

# ask: the exposed agent's answer (an agent-endpoint credential, e.g. a marketplace subscription)
client.ask("Summarise what the seller learned about Postgres RLS.")
```

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="TypeScript">

```ts
const doc = await client.add({ content: "Call notes with Acme: they want SSO before the pilot.",
                               title: "Call with Acme", customId: "call-2026-09-24" });
doc.id; doc.status;                              // "doc_…", "pending" or "processing"

const hits = await client.search({ q: "what does Acme need before the pilot", limit: 5 });
for (const h of hits.items) console.log(h.memory_name, "·", h.content);
hits.partial;                                    // the Memories that could not answer

const p = await client.profile({ q: "working hours" });
p.static; p.dynamic; p.results;

await client.ask({ message: "Summarise what the seller learned about Postgres RLS." });
```

</TabItem>


</Tabs>


`add` hands raw material to the write target's folder and starts its learning; poll
`documents.get(id)` until every entry of its `learning` reads `succeeded` if you need to know.
`search` is retrieval, not an answer; `ask` is the answer. `search` takes `mode="fast"` for one
round of retrieval with no model call, for recall before every turn of an agent whose own model
judges what it is handed. What each verb does inside the account, and what code sees when the
person does something in the app, is on [Memory operations](/build/guides/memory-operations/).

## The resources

Every list answers `{items, has_more, partial}`: the newest `limit` (1–1000, default 100),
whether more were left out, and the Memories that could not answer. Ids are typed and opaque:
`mem_…` a fact, `doc_…` a document, `med_…` a photo or video.


<Tabs syncKey="lang">


<TabItem label="Python">

```python
client.capabilities()                           # {"actions": ["search", "memories.list", …], "memories": [{name, kind}], …}

client.memories.list(limit=20)                  # the newest facts, each with its mem_ id and memory_name
client.memories.get("mem_…")
client.memories.add("We settled on Postgres.")  # a fact; the receipt is the note it was written as (doc_…, kind "note")
client.memories.forget("mem_…", confirm=True)

client.documents.list(kind="file")              # newest first; kind is "file" or "note"
client.documents.get("doc_…")                   # with learning: [{memory_name, status}]
client.documents.delete("doc_…", confirm=True)

client.media.list()                             # photos and videos in the media Memories in reach
client.media.search("someone skiing", kind="video")
client.media.get("med_…")                       # with its moments
client.media.delete("med_…", confirm=True)

client.rules()                                  # the user's standing rules for this credential
```

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="TypeScript">

```ts
await client.capabilities();

await client.memories.list({ limit: 20 });
await client.memories.get("mem_…");
await client.memories.add({ content: "We settled on Postgres." });
await client.memories.forget("mem_…", { confirm: true });

await client.documents.list({ kind: "file" });
await client.documents.get("doc_…");
await client.documents.delete("doc_…", { confirm: true });

await client.media.list();
await client.media.search({ q: "someone skiing", kind: "video" });
await client.media.get("med_…");
await client.media.delete("med_…", { confirm: true });

await client.rules();
```

</TabItem>


</Tabs>


`memories.add` answers the note it was written as (a `doc_…` of kind `note`): remove a note
with `documents.delete`. `memories.forget` takes the `mem_…` id of a learned fact, from
`memories.list`, `memories.get` or a search hit of `type: "memory"`; the material it was
learned from stays.

`delete` and `forget` need a key at **Full access**. Without `confirm` nothing changes and the
call raises `ConfirmationRequiredError` (HTTP `428 confirmation_required`), whose `details`
name the target (`id`, `verb`, …) and carry a `how` sentence to relay to the person. Pass
`confirm` only after they agreed; from a developer key that counts as the owner's confirmation.

## Errors

One class per HTTP status, all carrying the API's error envelope: `code` (which rule refused),
`message`, `details`, `retryable` and `trace_id` (quote it when reporting a problem).

| Status | Class | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `BadRequestError` | `code: validation`, from the service's own checks: an empty `q`, both or neither of `content` and `url`, a list `limit` outside 1–1000 |
| 401 | `AuthenticationError` | no bearer at all |
| 403 | `PermissionDeniedError` | `code: unauthorized`: an unknown, expired or revoked key, or a verb above its level |
| 404 | `NotFoundError` | an id that is not this key's to read: unknown, deleted, outside its reach or of the wrong type all answer alike |
| 409 | `ConflictError` | a conflicting write; retried automatically, then raised |
| 422 | `WriteTargetRequiredError` | `code: write_target_required`: a write from a key that reaches several text Memories and has no write target. Nothing was written; the key's owner decides where its writes go, no request can |
| 422 | `UnprocessableEntityError` | `code: validation` for a body the API cannot take: an unknown field (a `container`, a `metadata`), a missing or mistyped field, a search `limit` outside 1–50. `code: capability_unavailable`: the account's memory cannot run a turn here (no agent container, no model). Read `code`, not only the status |
| 428 | `ConfirmationRequiredError` | `code: confirmation_required`: a removal without `confirm`; nothing changed |
| 429 | `RateLimitError` | the account's concurrent-turn cap (two agent turns at once, reached by `forget` and `ask`), the service-wide ceiling on turns running at once (`details.scope: "process"`), or the per-token request limiter (`details.limit_per_min`); no `Retry-After` is sent; retried automatically with backoff, then raised. The per-token limiter covers every call, `search` and `add` included; the two-turn cap does not reach them. `add` and `memories.add` also raise it with `code: quota_exceeded` when the account's storage is full or its plan is not active; retrying does not help |
| 5xx | `InternalServerError` | retried automatically, then raised |
| — | `APIConnectionError`, `APITimeoutError` | the request never got an answer |


<Tabs syncKey="lang">


<TabItem label="Python">

```python
from membase import ConfirmationRequiredError, WriteTargetRequiredError

try:
    client.memories.forget("mem_…")
except ConfirmationRequiredError as e:
    print(e.code, e.details["how"], e.trace_id)    # confirmation_required  Pass confirm=true …  …

try:
    client.memories.add("We settled on Postgres.")
except WriteTargetRequiredError as e:
    print(e.message)                             # the key reaches several Memories and has no write target
```

</TabItem>



<TabItem label="TypeScript">

```ts
import { ConfirmationRequiredError, WriteTargetRequiredError } from "@unibaseio/membase";

try {
  await client.memories.forget("mem_…");
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof ConfirmationRequiredError) console.log(e.code, e.details, e.traceId);
}

try {
  await client.memories.add({ content: "We settled on Postgres." });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof WriteTargetRequiredError) console.log(e.message);
}
```

</TabItem>


</Tabs>


## Rules of the road

* **Reach is account state.** The Memories a key may use are switched on the Connect page. A key narrowed there stops reading a Memory on its very next call, with the same token: searches and lists leave it out, and its ids answer `404`.
* **No request names a Memory.** There is no `container` to pass; sending one is a `422`. Writes go to the key's write target.
* **Confirm means the person agreed.** Never pass `confirm` on your own initiative.
* **Writes are raw material.** `add` hands bytes to the write target's folder; its agent reads them in the next learning turn.
* **Do not store to filter later.** There are no server-side metadata filters on search; put what matters in the content, and use `custom_id` for your own bookkeeping.
* **The token stays out of logs.** Log the key's hint (`mbk_7f3a92d1…`) from the key's page, never the token.

## Method map

| SDK | REST | Protocol tool | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search(q, limit=, mode=)` | `POST /v1/search` | `search_memories` | Read |
| `add(...)`, `documents.add(...)` | `POST /v1/documents/add` | `add_document` | Read & write |
| `profile(q=…)` | `GET /v1/profile` | `get_profile` | Read + profile tick |
| `ask(message)` | `POST /v1/ask` | `ask_agent` | agent exposure |
| `rules()` | `GET /v1/rules` | `memory_rules` | Read |
| `capabilities()` | `GET /v1/capabilities` | — | any key |
| `memories.list(limit=)` | `GET /v1/memories` | `list_memories` (REST only) | Read |
| `memories.get(id)` | `GET /v1/memories/{id}` | `get_memory` (REST only) | Read |
| `memories.add(content, title=)` | `POST /v1/memories/add` | `add_memory` | Read & write |
| `memories.forget(id, confirm=True)` | `POST /v1/memories/{id}/forget` | `forget_memory` | Full access |
| `documents.list(kind=, limit=)` | `GET /v1/documents` | `list_documents` | Read |
| `documents.get(id)` | `GET /v1/documents/{id}` | `get_document` (REST only) | Read |
| `documents.delete(id, confirm=True)` | `POST /v1/documents/{id}/delete` | `delete_document` | Full access |
| `media.list(limit=)` | `GET /v1/media` | `list_media` | Read |
| `media.get(id)` | `GET /v1/media/{id}` | `get_media` | Read |
| `media.search(q, kind=, limit=)` | `POST /v1/media/search` | `search_media` | Read |
| `media.delete(id, confirm=True)` | `POST /v1/media/{id}/delete` | `delete_media` | Full access |

The MCP server offers the same operations under the protocol tool names, so a model that
learned `search_memories` in Claude is calling what your code calls `search`. Its tools still
take a `container` and offer `list_containers`; the REST API and the SDKs have neither.

## Without the SDK

Any HTTP client works. The OpenAPI document types the request bodies only: every response is
an untyped JSON object, and it names no server or auth scheme, so set the base URL
(`https://api.app.membase.com`) and the `Authorization: Bearer` header yourself:

```bash
npx openapi-typescript https://app.membase.com/plugin/openapi/agent-protocol.json -o membase.d.ts
```
